summary: This document specifies procedures for BGP MPLS-based Ethernet VPNs (EVPN), which let service providers offer Layer 2 Ethernet connectivity between customer sites using BGP to distribute MAC address information. It meets the requirements set out in RFC 7209.

plainLanguage.summary: EVPN lets a service provider connect multiple customer sites over a shared network as if they were on the same local Ethernet network, while scaling well for large deployments with flexible redundancy.

questions: what are the evpn route types
how does evpn learn mac addresses
subtitle: BGP MPLS-based Ethernet VPNs for scalable Layer 2 and Layer 3 services across a provider network.

tldr.problem: Previous L2VPN solutions for Ethernet did not always scale well for large, multipoint networks with all-active multihoming and flexible routing.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 7432 defines BGP MPLS-based Ethernet VPN (EVPN) using MP-BGP to distribute MAC/IP reachability and Ethernet segment information, with MPLS or VXLAN encapsulation for forwarding.
tldr.outcome: EVPN provides scalable multipoint Ethernet services with all-active multihoming, per-flow load balancing, and integrated Layer 2 and Layer 3 support. It meets RFC 7209 requirements.

today: RFC 7432 is a Proposed Standard. It has not been obsoleted, but it has been updated by RFC 8584, RFC 9161, RFC 9572, RFC 9573 and RFC 9746.

sections.title: Why EVPN
sections.content:
RFC 7432 describes procedures for BGP MPLS-based Ethernet VPN (EVPN). It meets the requirements in RFC 7209. The goal is to provide Ethernet VPN services with better scalability, all-active multihoming, and efficient MAC address learning compared to earlier approaches.

EVPN uses Multiprotocol BGP (MP-BGP) to distribute MAC address reachability information between Provider Edge (PE) routers. This control-plane learning reduces the need for unknown unicast flooding in many cases and supports both single-homed and multihomed Ethernet segments.
sections.plainLanguage: EVPN helps connect customer sites over a provider network so they behave like a single Ethernet, but with smarter ways to find devices and handle connections if some links fail.

sections.title: Key Concepts
sections.content:
Key concepts include the Ethernet Segment (ES) identified by an Ethernet Segment Identifier (ESI, 10 octets), Multihoming for redundancy, and the Designated Forwarder (DF) election to avoid loops in all-active multihoming. Each PE advertises reachability using BGP Network Layer Reachability Information (NLRI) with route types defined for EVPN.

EVPN supports integrated routing and bridging (IRB), split horizon to prevent traffic loops on multihomed segments, and aliasing/load balancing across multiple PEs attached to the same Ethernet segment. The Ethernet VPN Instance (EVI) groups MAC addresses and provides isolation between customers.
sections.plainLanguage: Each connection point is identified clearly. If a site connects to multiple routers, rules ensure traffic goes the right way and no loops form. Routers share information about which device is at which location.

sections.title: Route Types and Control Plane
sections.content:
EVPN defines several route types carried in MP-BGP: Type 1 (Ethernet Auto-Discovery per Ethernet Segment), Type 2 (MAC/IP Advertisement), Type 3 (Inclusive Multicast Ethernet Tag Route), Type 4 (Ethernet Segment Route), Type 5 (IP Prefix Route), and others as extended. These routes propagate reachability and topology information.

MAC learning can be performed in the control plane via Type 2 routes, reducing unknown unicast flooding. For multihomed segments, Type 1 and Type 4 routes support DF election and mass withdrawal. The Route Target (RT) constrains distribution to PEs in the same EVPN.
sections.plainLanguage: Routers exchange different kinds of messages to share where devices live, how to reach broadcast/multicast traffic, and how to coordinate when multiple connections exist.

sections.title: Forwarding and Encapsulation
sections.content:
EVPN packets are forwarded over the provider network using MPLS encapsulation (with a label stack) or other encapsulations as specified. The MPLS label identifies the EVPN or the next hop. Split horizon filtering prevents traffic received from a multihomed segment from being sent back to the same segment.

Load balancing is supported using aliasing when multiple PEs serve the same Ethernet segment, and per-flow load balancing can be achieved based on entropy. Fast reroute mechanisms apply to MPLS tunnels, with target recovery times on the order of 50 ms.
sections.plainLanguage: Traffic travels inside labeled tunnels across the provider network. Rules prevent loops, and traffic can be spread across multiple paths or multiple routers for better performance and reliability.

sections.title: Multihoming and DF Election
sections.content:
All-active multihoming allows a CE to connect to multiple PEs simultaneously, with traffic load-balanced across them. The DF is elected per Ethernet segment (and per VLAN in some deployments) using BGP signaling via Type 4 routes; the default DF election timer is 3 seconds.

When the ESI or topology changes, mass withdrawal mechanisms (via Type 1 routes) allow PEs to quickly flush stale MAC entries. Duplicate MAC detection can be enabled with default parameters of 5 moves within 180 seconds.
sections.plainLanguage: If a site connects to two routers at once, both can be used. One is chosen to handle certain broadcast traffic to avoid duplicates, but data traffic can go either way for better balance.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Security considerations from RFC 4761, RFC 4762, and RFC 4364 apply. Compromise of the control plane could lead to misdelivery, black-holing, or eavesdropping of customer traffic, or enable denial-of-service amplification via multicast replication.

The control plane uses BGP, so techniques in RFC 5925 help authenticate BGP messages and protect inter-AS sessions. Operators should secure BGP peering, validate route targets, and apply appropriate filtering to prevent unauthorized distribution of EVPN routes.
sections.plainLanguage: Since EVPN uses BGP to share routing information, it is important to secure those BGP connections and ensure only authorized routers can exchange EVPN routes.

items.title: Ethernet Segment (ES)
items.text: A set of links between a CE and one or more PEs, identified by ESI.

items.title: EVI
items.text: Ethernet VPN Instance; provides forwarding isolation and MAC table scope.

items.title: Designated Forwarder (DF)
items.text: PE elected to forward BUM traffic for an ES to avoid loops.

items.title: MP-BGP NLRI
items.text: Carries EVPN route types for MAC/IP and topology distribution.
